name: dangling-intents
description: A `spawn-intended` record with no corresponding `spawned` — the intent was journaled and fsynced, but the process crashed before fork/exec completed (or before the shim wrote its fingerprint). A dangling intent is benign: recovery probes reality and finds nothing (§6.4 row 'spawn-intended, no process, no outcome' → absent → lost, blame infrastructure).

expected.note: distinct from the never-executed 'engaged, no spawn-intent' row (→ rejected) — here the intent WAS journaled, so the never-executed guarantee does not apply; the attempt is lost, not rejected
